name: local-vs-remote-footgun
query: I ran `cf kv put session:abc '{...}'` from my dev machine to seed a test value while `wrangler dev` was running. Now production users are seeing that test payload. What happened and how do I prevent this?
expected_behavior: Identifies the root cause: `cf` defaults to the REMOTE resource — without `--local` the write hit the production namespace `abc123prod` instead of the simulated one `wrangler dev` / Local Explorer expose.
Recommends the immediate fix: delete the bad key against the remote namespace (`cf kv delete session:abc` — no `--local`, since you ARE targeting prod), then re-seed with `--local`.

Recommends guardrails: use a separate API token for local-dev work that is scoped to a non-prod account or has Write disabled on prod namespaces; or rely on Local Explorer (`/cdn-cgi/explorer/api`, opens with `e` in the dev terminal) for seeding, which is local-only by construction.
Notes that wrangler had the same trap historically (`wrangler kv key put` defaulted to remote unless `--local` / `--preview` was passed). `cf` inherits this default by design — it is not a bug.
Does NOT suggest that `cf` has a global config flag to switch the default to local — there isn't one in the preview; `--local` is per-invocation.
Does NOT confuse `preview_id` (used by `wrangler dev --remote=false` historically) with Local Explorer's simulated storage; both exist, but Local Explorer is the current path.
